why: Recorded for the README video, from its script, fixed before recording: the sprint review is one task of five prompts (outline, check against the tickets, fix, build on the template, check the slides), and in the takes the action items and the LinkedIn post before it are a task each, starting at prompts 3 and 5. lucazagaia/skycast is a demo repo made for the recording; its milestones, issues and pull requests are invented, and notes/ holds copies of recording/meeting-1.md and recording/notes.md. Level same-goal: the runs were made to be alike. recurrence.py sets levels per session, so the takes' post and action items count as another subject against P-F and P-2said, which read the same notes.
history: Recorded 2026-09-23 and 24 for the README video. Held out while the boundary question was restructured, and judged only after: every switch found, no false cut (docs/research/benchmarks.md, "The question restructured"). Published 2026-09-25.

Rechecked each bullet against the fetched data. Four bullets aren't backed:

**Slide 4 — "originally raised as #3"**
Issue #3 *"Temperatures show in Fahrenheit outside the US"* belongs to **Sprint 1** and was already addressed there by PR #4 *"Pick the temperature unit from the region."* So framing #10/#11 as the fix for #3 is wrong — #10 is a follow-on feature, not the same complaint.

**Slide 5 — "unblocks Sprint 3 work"**
Pure speculation. Nothing in PR #12's title or metadata (or any Sprint 3 item I fetched) says it was a prerequisite.

**Slide 6 — "Sprint 3 already underway — 4 items closed, 1 open"**
The milestone counts say **7 closed, 1 open**, not 4/1. I based "4" on the four items that surfaced in my search results, but the milestone metadata is authoritative and I hadn't fetched the rest.

**Slide 6 — "all 4 PRs merged"**
I only queried `state=closed` / `closed_at`; I didn't pull the `merged`/`merged_at` fields. Closed ≠ merged on GitHub (a closed PR could have been rejected). Very likely all merged, but not verified.

Also worth flagging as **inferred but not directly verified** (not wrong, just not proven by what I fetched):
- The PR→issue "closes" links on slide 3 (#7→#6, #9→#8) — I matched by title, didn't check the PR bodies for `Closes #N`.
- Which specific issues sat on the Sprint 2 milestone — I never queried issue-level milestone; I inferred #6/#8/#10 because 3 issues + 4 PRs = the milestone's 7 closed items and the titles line up.
- Slide 2's narrative framing of the sprint goal is my paraphrase, not a quoted goal.
